Humans review every outbound message.</p><p>Here are some of the real workflows Legal Ops runs with Grok Bot today.</p><h2 id="counsel-11-prep-and-writeback"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#counsel-11-prep-and-writeback">Counsel 1:1 prep and writeback</a></h2><h3 id="what-it-does"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#what-it-does">What it does</a></h3><p>Before recurring attorney 1:1s, Grok Bot reviews Slack, Notion, meeting notes, and trackers, then drafts a focused agenda with open questions, cross-channel contradictions, blockers, and wins. After the meeting, it writes decisions and follow-ups back to the right Notion pages and trackers.</p><h3 id="why-it-matters"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#why-it-matters">Why it matters</a></h3><p>Counsel time stays focused on decisions, not archaeology, and preparation stays consistent week to week.</p><h2 id="legal-slack-triage-answer-consistency-and-legal-review-tracker"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#legal-slack-triage-answer-consistency-and-legal-review-tracker">Legal Slack triage, answer consistency, and Legal Review tracker</a></h2><h3 id="what-it-does-1"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#what-it-does-1">What it does</a></h3><p>Slack triage: this bot watches legal and GTM-legal traffic for unanswered questions, conflicting guidance, and recurring topics (paper path, BAA coverage, entity questions). It surfaces those for Legal Ops and counsel so threads don&#x27;t stall or get contradictory answers.</p><p>Legal Review tracker: this bot maintains a tracker from GTM-legal Slack intakes. It classifies open asks (Needs Legal, re-look, approval bands), refreshes on a schedule, and enriches open Needs Legal rows with attorney-ready context: live Slack thread summaries, Salesforce Opportunity and Primary Quote snapshots, related Deal Desk signals, and linked prior guidance.</p><p>How we got here: that tracker previously ran on Cursor automation plus Google Apps Script. Refresh, enrichment, and digests now run in Grok Bot.</p><h3 id="why-it-matters-1"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#why-it-matters-1">Why it matters</a></h3><p>Sales and Deal Desk get one clear item and Legal Ops sees pattern risk early. Counsel can answer business asks from one sheet instead of rebuilding the deal from Slack and Salesforce.</p><h2 id="contract-lifecycle--ironclad-support"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#contract-lifecycle--ironclad-support">Contract lifecycle / Ironclad support</a></h2><h3 id="what-it-does-2"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#what-it-does-2">What it does</a></h3><p>Grok Bot looks up workflows, statuses, and documents in the contract system; summarizes open reviews; and, on explicit request, helps move counsel-approved documents from Slack into the right contract workflow, with preview and confirmation before any write.</p><h3 id="why-it-matters-2"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#why-it-matters-2">Why it matters</a></h3><p>Handoffs from negotiation chat into the system of record are faster, without silent changes.</p><h2 id="more-workflows"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#more-workflows">More workflows</a></h2><h3 id="deal-and-salesforce-context-for-legal-questions"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#deal-and-salesforce-context-for-legal-questions">Deal and Salesforce context for legal questions</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>What it does:</strong> When Legal needs to answer a GTM question about agreements, Grok Bot pulls opportunity and account context so advice matches the actual deal.</li>
<li><strong>Why it matters:</strong> Paper and agreement guidance depend on product mix and deal stage. Wrong assumptions create bad customer promises.</li>
</ul><h3 id="procurement-and-vendor-workflow-analytics"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#procurement-and-vendor-workflow-analytics">Procurement and vendor workflow analytics</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>What it does:</strong> Grok Bot maps procurement tickets to teams, measures review cycle times, attributes waiting time among requester, Legal, and counterparty, and drafts GC-ready memos and Sheets from contract-system exports, with source verification and plain-language statistics.</li>
<li><strong>Why it matters:</strong> Leadership sees where work actually sits, without turning analysis into a narrative about individual performance.</li>
</ul><h3 id="legal-templates-tracker-hygiene"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#legal-templates-tracker-hygiene">Legal templates tracker hygiene</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>What it does:</strong> Grok Bot keeps a living inventory of legal templates across Drive, Notion, and Slack candidates, flags new or updated templates, and runs sync health checks so current templates remain trustworthy.</li>
<li><strong>Why it matters:</strong> GTM and Legal stop shipping stale forms.</li>
</ul><h3 id="executive--weekly-legal-ops-reporting"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#executive--weekly-legal-ops-reporting">Executive / weekly Legal Ops reporting</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>What it does:</strong> Grok Bot drafts Legal Ops updates from Slack, Notion, meeting notes, and calendar context. It also posts a lightweight team reminder so updates go out on time.</li>
<li><strong>Why it matters:</strong> Leadership gets a coherent weekly picture without rebuilding it from scratch.</li>
</ul><h3 id="channel-routing-and-deprecation-hygiene"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#channel-routing-and-deprecation-hygiene">Channel routing and deprecation hygiene</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>What it does:</strong> When people post in a retired GTM channel, an agent redirects them to the current legal intake channel with a short, consistent message.</li>
<li><strong>Why it matters:</strong> There are fewer lost requests after Slack migrations and channel retirements.</li>
</ul><h3 id="disclosure--finsys-executive-views-as-needed"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#disclosure--finsys-executive-views-as-needed">Disclosure / Finsys executive views (as needed)</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>What it does:</strong> Grok Bot builds simple executive dashboard views on Legal Ops trackers, such as disclosure classifications and counts, without altering underlying analysis cells.</li>
<li><strong>Why it matters:</strong> Counsel leadership gets board-ready snapshots.</li>
</ul><h3 id="controls--audit-style-reviews-as-needed"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#controls--audit-style-reviews-as-needed">Controls / audit-style reviews (as needed)</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>What it does:</strong> Grok Bot acts as a skeptical reviewer on revenue contracting controls, SOX-relevant design questions, and evidence gaps, challenging assumptions and citing sources.</li>
<li><strong>Why it matters:</strong> Legal Ops stress-tests process design before auditors do.</li>
</ul><h3 id="day-to-day-general-counsel-ops-assistant"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#day-to-day-general-counsel-ops-assistant">Day-to-day general counsel ops assistant</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>What it does:</strong> Grok Bot researches across Slack, Notion, meeting notes, and Drive; drafts Slack replies and customer-safe talk tracks; compares contract language; summarizes handbooks and policies; prepares 1:1 packs; never invents facts; and drafts rather than sends unless asked.</li>
<li><strong>Why it matters:</strong> One careful generalist handles work that does not fit a specialist bot.</li>
</ul><h2 id="pros-of-moving-to-grok-bot"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#pros-of-moving-to-grok-bot">Pros of moving to Grok Bot</a></h2><ul>
<li>All logic lives in Grok Bot. We can update rules and enrichment without editing Apps Script or redeploying Cursor automation.</li>
<li>Richer attorney-facing enrichment on open Needs Legal rows (thread summary, Salesforce Snapshot, Deal Desk context, linked guidance).</li>
<li>Faster iteration: change a skill or routine and the next refresh picks it up.</li>
<li>One agent owns the ~30-minute refresh, twice-daily commercial enrich, and Monday open-items digest.</li>
<li>Formatting and Snapshot language stay consistent because prompts and skills are editable in chat.</li>
</ul><h2 id="patterns-that-travel-well-to-other-legal-teams"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#patterns-that-travel-well-to-other-legal-teams">Patterns that travel well to other legal teams</a></h2><ol class="[&amp;&gt;li]:marker:content-[counters(list-item,&#x27;.&#x27;)_&#x27;._&#x27;]">
<li>Specialize agents by workflow: prep, triage, contracts, and templates, not one mega-bot for everything.</li>
<li>Prefer draft, then human send, for external or Slack messages.</li>
<li>Automate recurring preparation and writeback on a calendar; keep research on demand.</li>
<li>Put standing rules in memory: verify sources, make no assumptions, and use plain language.</li>
<li>Separate read paths from write paths for systems of record such as contracts and Salesforce.</li>
</ol></div></div><div class="text-primary/40 mt-12 text-sm leading-7"><span aria-hidden="true">—</span><br/>Written by <!-- -->Kelly Noguchi</div></article><section class="mt-24 sm:mt-32"><div
